proof_mechanisms: 1. Identify blocks of length ~14 (x0 in [4..17] is block 1, [18..31] is block 2)
2. Within each block, even-indexed entries decrease and odd-indexed entries increase
3. At block boundaries, values jump and scale
4. Check if the scaling factor matches a triangular or multiplicative rule
claim.statement: Parents 5,6,7 correctly matched x0=8..17 with the pattern even->decreasing, odd->increasing. But they fail at x0=18 because a new 'block' starts. The jump from x0=17->25 to x0=18->43 suggests blocks scale. Block 1 (x0=8..17): even goes 12,11,10,9,8; odd goes 21,22,23,24,25. Block 2 starts at x0=18 with even at 43 and odd at 62. This hypothesis tries block-based scaling.
